results.name: prev_yes_carryover
results.description: Over consecutive within-session trial pairs (trial_index increments by 1), P(yes | previous yes) minus P(yes | previous no); observed above the null means sequential response perseveration that the trial-independent model under-produces, below means alternation.

results.name: ones_digit_set_tens_digit_leak
results.description: Among sets of >=2 examples all sharing a nonzero ones digit d, the yes rate to non-example targets that contain d only in the tens place (e.g. 70-79 after 97,77,87,47); observed above the null means people generalize to the "contains digit d" rule more than the model predicts, below means the model over-weights "contains d".
results.code:
# name: ones_digit_set_tens_digit_leak
# description: Among sets of >=2 examples all sharing a nonzero ones digit d, the yes rate to non-example targets that contain d only in the tens place (e.g. 70-79 after 97,77,87,47); observed above the null means people generalize to the "contains digit d" rule more than the model predicts, below means the model over-weights "contains d".
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",")
    ones = ex.map(lambda e: {int(x) % 10 for x in e})
    n = ex.map(len).to_numpy()
    shared = ones.map(lambda s: next(iter(s)) if len(s) == 1 else -1).to_numpy()
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    isex = np.array([str(a) in b for a, b in zip(t, ex)])
    m = (n >= 2) & (shared > 0) & (t // 10 == shared) & (t % 10 != shared) & ~isex
    if m.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(df["rating"].to_numpy()[m].mean())

results.name: pow2_set_even_leak_rate
results.description: Among sets whose examples are all powers of 2 (2..64), the yes rate to even non-example targets that are NOT powers of 2; observed above the null means people still leak to "even numbers" more than the size-weighted rule prior predicts (model over-commits to powers of 2), below means the model over-generalizes to evens.

results.name: multiple_of_k_set_rule_contrast
results.description: Among sets of >=2 examples whose gcd k is 3..12 and that do not share a ones digit, yes rate to non-example multiples of k minus yes rate to non-multiples; observed above the null means people commit to the "multiples of k" rule more sharply than the model predicts, below means the model over-commits to it.
results.code:
# name: multiple_of_k_set_rule_contrast
# description: Among sets of >=2 examples whose gcd k is 3..12 and that do not share a ones digit, yes rate to non-example multiples of k minus yes rate to non-multiples; observed above the null means people commit to the "multiples of k" rule more sharply than the model predicts, below means the model over-commits to it.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",")
    vals = ex.map(lambda e: [int(x) for x in e])
    n = vals.map(len).to_numpy()
    g = vals.map(lambda v: math.gcd(*v) if len(v) > 1 else 0).to_numpy()
    shared = vals.map(lambda v: len({x % 10 for x in v}) == 1).to_numpy()
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    isex = np.array([a in v for a, v in zip(t, vals)])
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy()
    base = (n >= 2) & (g >= 3) & (g <= 12) & ~shared & ~isex
    gs = np.where(g > 0, g, 1)
    mm, mn = base & (t % gs == 0), base & (t % gs != 0)
    if mm.sum() == 0 or mn.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[mm].mean() - r[mn].mean())

results.name: square_set_square_target_rate
results.description: Among sets of >=2 examples that are all perfect squares, yes rate to non-example square targets minus yes rate to non-square targets; observed above the null means people pick up "square numbers" more sharply than the model predicts, below means the model over-commits to squares.
results.code:
# name: square_set_square_target_rate
# description: Among sets of >=2 examples that are all perfect squares, yes rate to non-example square targets minus yes rate to non-square targets; observed above the null means people pick up "square numbers" more sharply than the model predicts, below means the model over-commits to squares.
def test_statistic(df):
    sq = {i * i for i in range(1, 11)}
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",")
    vals = ex.map(lambda e: [int(x) for x in e])
    n = vals.map(len).to_numpy()
    allsq = vals.map(lambda v: all(x in sq for x in v)).to_numpy()
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    isex = np.array([a in v for a, v in zip(t, vals)])
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy()
    issq = np.isin(t, list(sq))
    base = (n >= 2) & allsq & ~isex
    ms, mn = base & issq, base & ~issq
    if ms.sum() == 0 or mn.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[ms].mean() - r[mn].mean())

results.name: ones_digit_set_unrelated_target_rate
results.description: Among sets of >=2 examples all sharing a ones digit d (incl. multiples of 10), the yes rate to targets that neither end in d nor contain d at all; observed above the null means people's yes responses leak beyond the digit rule (via ranges/parity) more than the model predicts, below means the model leaks too much.
results.code:
# name: ones_digit_set_unrelated_target_rate
# description: Among sets of >=2 examples all sharing a ones digit d (incl. multiples of 10), the yes rate to targets that neither end in d nor contain d at all; observed above the null means people's yes responses leak beyond the digit rule (via ranges/parity) more than the model predicts, below means the model leaks too much.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",")
    ones = ex.map(lambda e: {int(x) % 10 for x in e})
    n = ex.map(len).to_numpy()
    shared = ones.map(lambda s: next(iter(s)) if len(s) == 1 else -1).to_numpy()
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    tens = t // 10
    m = (n >= 2) & (shared >= 0) & (t % 10 != shared) & ((tens != shared) | (shared == 0)) & (t != 100)
    if m.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(df["rating"].to_numpy()[m].mean())

results.name: single_example_shared_digit_contrast
results.description: Among single-example sets, yes rate to non-example targets sharing a digit (tens or ones, as a digit string) with the example minus yes rate to targets sharing no digit; observed above the null means people generalize from one number by digit similarity more than the model predicts, below means the model over-weights digit rules.
results.code:
# name: single_example_shared_digit_contrast
# description: Among single-example sets, yes rate to non-example targets sharing a digit (tens or ones, as a digit string) with the example minus yes rate to targets sharing no digit; observed above the null means people generalize from one number by digit similarity more than the model predicts, below means the model over-weights digit rules.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    single = ~s.str.contains(",").to_numpy()
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    ts = t.astype(str).to_numpy()
    sv = s.to_numpy()
    share = np.array([bool(set(a) & set(b)) for a, b in zip(ts, sv)])
    isex = ts == sv
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy()
    ms, mn = single & share & ~isex, single & ~share
    if ms.sum() == 0 or mn.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[ms].mean() - r[mn].mean())

results.name: odd_set_parity_contrast
results.description: Among sets of >=2 all-odd examples that do NOT share a ones digit, yes rate to odd non-example targets minus yes rate to even targets; observed above the null means people use parity ("odd numbers") more sharply than the model predicts, below means the model over-weights parity.
results.code:
# name: odd_set_parity_contrast
# description: Among sets of >=2 all-odd examples that do NOT share a ones digit, yes rate to odd non-example targets minus yes rate to even targets; observed above the null means people use parity ("odd numbers") more sharply than the model predicts, below means the model over-weights parity.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",")
    vals = ex.map(lambda e: [int(x) for x in e])
    n = vals.map(len).to_numpy()
    allodd = vals.map(lambda v: all(x % 2 == 1 for x in v)).to_numpy()
    shared = vals.map(lambda v: len({x % 10 for x in v}) == 1).to_numpy()
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    isex = np.array([a in v for a, v in zip(t, vals)])
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy()
    base = (n >= 2) & allodd & ~shared & ~isex
    mo, me = base & (t % 2 == 1), base & (t % 2 == 0)
    if mo.sum() == 0 or me.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[mo].mean() - r[me].mean())
